reviewer: Scout, advancement session 2026-10-29 (review over the accepted ns-bwa-001 artifact e8ed2a53eaf0453c, gate 1.5.0 46/46, re-accepted in jobs ns-bwa-baseline-001 and ns-bwa-diag-001; every reference and model figure replicated by the ns-bwa-diag-001 second implementation)
summary: Retained for retrospective model-development research under an isolated-rows protocol that is STATED AS A REQUIREMENT, not enforced by the shipped runner: the illustrative runner contract passes the whole eval feature table to the predictor, and the gate's own declared probes measured the cross-row exposure (site-level reverse-history covers 369 train / 56 eval / 217 holdout rows - a later same-site row's site_prior_lift30_rate equals the earlier row's label when that prior is its only resolved one), so unrestricted-access scores are not meaningful for this artifact. The register is revised in place and publishes no historical vintages, so training-label timing and full-row historical availability are unverified; the vintage is the pinned 2026-06-16 snapshot and the task is declared retrospective, never a point-in-time reconstruction. Measured finding carried beside every figure: the stock runner baseline (eval AUC 0.5086) trails the shipped site-persistence reference (0.6124) by 0.1038 with paired intervals excluding zero at both the row and site-cluster level - no demonstrated headroom under this protocol; the comparison, not the top-line AUC, is the release's scientific content.
supported_uses: Retrospective research and method comparison on the pinned 2026-06-16 vintage under an enforced isolated-rows protocol (one row predicted without any other row)
Agent evaluation under the same enforced protocol, with the labeled eval split as development/validation data and the holdout kept outside agent development until a design is frozen
Study of advisory-duration regime shift (the measured 2020-2022 spike) and of prevalence drift under a temporal split
unsupported_uses: Operational or real-time forecasting claims: no historical-vintage availability evidence exists and none is claimed
Point-in-time historical reconstruction: the publisher revises in place; a future re-fetch measures churn, not past knowability
Any evaluation that gives the predictor whole-table access to eval or holdout features: the measured same-site label recovery makes such scores meaningless
Quoting the model AUC (0.5086) without the persistence comparison (0.6124, intervals excluding zero) beside it

cross_row_audit.scope: gate-executed reverse-history probes on the full artifact: site-level coverage 369 train / 56 eval / 217 holdout rows (a later same-site row's prior-lift-rate equals the earlier row's label when that prior is its only resolved one; 1 mismatch in train), county-level 109/18/3 with more mismatches; mitigated only by the declared isolated-rows protocol, which the shipped runner does not enforce
evidence: The gate's own qualification report for this artifact records both declared probes executed with their measured per-split coverage (46/46 checks passed, including evaluation_contract and both probes).

Job ns-bwa-diag-001 preserved per-row model and persistence scores on the accepted bytes and computed the model-vs-persistence paired intervals (row -0.1035 [-0.1693, -0.0357]; site-cluster -0.1028 [-0.1706, -0.0383]), both excluding zero, on the same 372 eval rows.

limitations: Single pinned vintage (register content current as of 2026-06-16); the publisher updates quarterly and revises in place, so no historical operational-availability claim is possible
The measured cross-row exposure means eval scores under unrestricted table access are not meaningful; the isolated-rows requirement must be enforced by the evaluator

No demonstrated headroom: the stock baseline trails the site-persistence reference with intervals excluding zero; the task's discriminative claim above simple references is not established by the runner's own baseline
Prevalence shift inside eval (0.744 in 2018 to 0.415 in 2020) and the 2020-2022 duration-regime spike inside holdout make pooled figures unrepresentative; per-issue-year tables are mandatory reading

Site identity is register free text with variants (no clean entity key); history features use a stated normalisation rule and 19 same-(site, issue date) pairs + 1 triple exist (16 pairs with two valid durations - label noise, counted)
The holdout was never evaluated; no holdout figure exists and its first use must follow a frozen design
